A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same auction-coordination research. All pages, including Appendices A–D, are readable, and the equations, tables and figures support comparison across the substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original simulations using synthetic distributions and the iPinYou empirical price distribution, with results in Section 6, Table 1 and Figures 1–3, including Appendix D.

after.justification: V2 retains original simulation results for synthetic and iPinYou-based settings in Section 6, Table 1 and Figures 1–5, including Appendix D.

M1.justification: Algorithm 3 generalizes v1's exponential multiplier update to a Bregman-divergence update parameterized by a Legendre mirror map. This permits different update procedures; the entropy update becomes a special case. Highest-value coordination remains unchanged, and all reported experiments still use the entropy case.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three symmetric synthetic scenarios, three asymmetric synthetic scenarios and two iPinYou-based coalition sizes. The distributions, represented tasks and Season 2 test data are retained; relocated figures do not introduce additional coverage.

E2.justification: The reported comparisons remain independent versus coordinated bidding using the same entropy-based auto-bidder. Arbitrary coordination mechanisms are introduced as theoretical comparators, without additional empirical baseline evaluations.

E3.justification: Section 6.2 reduces the reported evaluation metrics from utility, achieved value and multiplier to utility and achieved value. The matched scenarios retain their coalition sizes, auction horizons, learning rate, data sampling and preprocessing.

E4.justification: V2 removes the multiplier-trajectory diagnostics from every experimental scenario and the associated empirical convergence-to-zero findings. The heterogeneous-bidder analyses remain, and no new ablations or robustness studies replace the removed convergence evidence.

E5.justification: The stated 95% confidence-interval formula changes from mean ± 1.96 times the simulation standard deviation to mean ± 1.96 times standard deviation divided by sqrt(100). Both versions report 100 simulations. Table 1 also changes its interval-suppression threshold from below 0.002 to at most 0.0025. These revisions do not establish additional runs.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises several values under retained settings. For the four-bidder iPinYou experiment, independent value changes from 0.614 to 0.620 and coordinated value from 0.929 to 0.928; symmetric four-bidder independent value changes from 0.773 to 0.774. Coordination's aggregate ranking remains unchanged. Multiplier trajectories and their empirical convergence findings are removed.

T1.justification: V2 changes Assumption 1 from a strictly positive margin to Delta ≥ 0, adds a necessity counterexample and a large-coalition sufficiency argument, and explicitly requires full-support valuations. It introduces general mirror-map definitions, value dominance without Assumption 1, and optimality against arbitrary coordination mechanisms, with extensive new or generalized proofs. V1's i.i.d. high-probability utility bound survives as Remark 3.1.

C1.justification: The contributions expand from sufficient conditions for one entropy-based algorithm to a necessary-and-sufficient RoS condition, value dominance for a broader mirror-descent class without Assumption 1, and asymptotic optimality among coordination mechanisms. The abstract also removes v1's blanket wording about strict value improvement for each participant.

C2.justification: V2 adds a stable-reference-point explanation allowing a positive limiting multiplier, beyond v1's zero-multiplier argument under competitiveness. Failure of Assumption 1 becomes a substantive adverse-RoS regime rather than an uninteresting case. New discussion addresses utility redistribution, inaccessible private valuations and why the available iPinYou information does not support their proposed non-i.i.d. modeling.

D1.justification: Table 1 newly specifies that all totals are normalized by the auction horizon T, clarifying previously undocumented aggregation. The data-processing instructions remain unchanged, and neither version supplies code access, hardware specifications or runtime information.

R1.justification: V2 adds Balseiro, Lu and Mirrokni's 2023 work on dual mirror descent to support the broader algorithmic framing. The previous cited works and the central positioning around coordinating value maximizers rather than utility maximizers remain.

P1.justification: The introduction and theoretical narrative are substantially rewritten. Lengthy main-text proofs move into appendices organized by section, while the main text gains proof sketches and explanatory claims. The experimental subsections and discussion are also reorganized; this extends beyond merely inserting new results.

P2.justification: The three original figure groups become five reorganized groups, with multiplier columns removed and utility/value panels paired and relabeled. Representative synthetic and real-data figures move beside the results discussion, with remaining panels redistributed in Appendix D. Typography, author layout, table caption placement and page composition also change throughout.

improvement.justification: V2 adds a useful necessity counterexample and corrects the stated confidence-interval formula, but central theoretical extensions contain new proof gaps. Appendix B.1, Equation (14), can have zero utility on the left and a negative right-hand side when the highest-value bidder loses internally. Appendices B.3/C.2 also use (h')^{-1}(delta) where h'(delta) is needed to infer lambda ≤ delta. These problems weaken support for the expanded claims, while empirical convergence diagnostics are removed. The benefits and harms do not establish a reliable net quality improvement.
